summary:
Trends is the category to trust blind right now — every rating is riding a 6-game winning streak on trends, hitting 82% (9-2) over the last 14 days across R1 through R4, dwarfing season baselines in the 56-59% range. Runs isn't far behind, with R2, R3, and R4 all on 4-game win streaks at 73% (8-3, n=11), while hitting has quietly strung together its own 4-game streaks at 64% across the board. The flip side is real: SP, bullpen, and bullpen_fatigue are all stuck at identical 45% (5-6, n=11) lines across every rating, a clear cold patch that's dragging on exactly the categories you'd lean on for a World Series Game 6. The combo data backs the hot side up — trends+sp leads all pairings at 57.9% (368-268) and trends+runs sits at 57.3% (402-300), so when trends agrees with a shakier category like sp, ride it.

Today's slate is just the one game, but it's a loaded one: Game 6, MIL @ TBR, and all four ratings converge hard on Milwaukee, with deltas stacking from -1.50 (R1, R4) to -1.81 (R3) — full consensus, no split. That's the kind of alignment the model's best category combo (trends+sp at 57.9%) would want backing it if trends is flashing green on this side, and given trends' 82% hot streak lately, a MIL lean here carries extra weight beyond the raw rating gap. Milwaukee's season profile as a liked team is elite — 49-22 (69%) outright and 27-12 (+18.0u) in strong-play spots — while Tampa Bay's own number as a liked team (44-19, 70%) means the model respects both sides, but today everything funnels to the Brewers. With R2 and R3 both showing strong-play profit over the last 30 days (+8.0u and +4.0u respectively) and R1 carrying a monster +84.0u season strong-play mark, if this MIL lean clears the strong-play delta threshold, it's the shape of play this model was built for — just keep in mind SP/bullpen metrics are ice cold right now, so don't let a close Gasser-Peralta pitching matchup override the trends/runs signal carrying the day.
